facts.program: Xcel Energy cold-climate air source heat pump
facts.claim: $750 per heating ton at 5°F standard; $1,500 per ton with the gas-home bonus
facts.eligibility: Xcel electric or gas customers in Colorado; participating contractor. Bonus for homes heated with Xcel natural gas, effective Oct 1, 2026. Electric-heat homes (e.g. baseboards) get the standard amount only.
facts.dates: Effective Oct 1, 2026; install invoiced by Dec 31, 2026, applications through Sep 30, 2027
facts.notes: The old $2,250 per ton / $9,000 figure came from an earlier rate sheet and is wrong for 2026.

facts.program: Xcel Energy air source heat pump (ducted)
facts.claim: $300 per cooling ton standard; $600 with bonus

facts.program: Xcel Energy heat pump water heater
facts.notes: The old $2,250 flat figure is wrong.

facts.program: Xcel Energy insulation and air sealing
facts.claim: 30% of cost: up to $500 attic, $350 wall, $400 air sealing; gas customers 1.5 times
facts.notes: Taken from the same rebate sheet as our /programs/xcel-energy-colorado-rebates/ page.

facts.program: Xcel Energy EV charger and wiring rebate
facts.claim: Up to $500 for a Level 2 charger and/or 240V wiring; standard rebate up to $800 in a Disproportionately Impacted Community; up to $2,300 income-qualified
facts.eligibility: Enroll in Optimize Your Charge first. EV Accelerate At Home closed to new Colorado applications on July 14, 2026.
facts.notes: The old '$1,300' figure added $500 + $800 and is wrong.

facts.claim: General: $250 per kW AC of max continuous discharge power, up to $5,000; income-qualified $1,000 per kW; DIC $500 per kW (IQ and DIC capped at 75% of equipment cost); plus $100 a year for 5 years
facts.eligibility: Tesla Powerwall or current Enphase batteries; solar-charged; Xcel controls the battery during peak events
facts.dates: Reopened May 21, 2026; general budget $13.6M with $11.3M left on Sep 1, 2026

facts.claim: 2026 residential products are income-qualified and Disproportionately Impacted Community only: $1 per watt up to 10 kW AC upfront. Everyone else gets net metering only, no upfront rebate.
facts.amount: $1 per watt up to 10 kW (IQ/DIC only)
facts.notes: The old '$300 per kW, up to $1,500' figure is wrong for general customers.
Applies to every state; do not show a 30% federal credit on 2026 installs.
